filename: Non‐Linear Dimensionality Reduction With a Variational Encoder Decoder to Understand Convective Processes in Climate Models - Behrens - 2022 - Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems.pdf
title: Non-Linear Dimensionality Reduction With a Variational Encoder Decoder to Understand Convective Processes in Climate Models
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
parameterization_target: total diabatic heating tendency, total diabatic moistening tendency, radiative fluxes (top and surface shortwave/longwave), and precipitation
testbed_rationale: Uses the established SPCAM aquaplanet simulation benchmark (originating from Rasp et al., 2018 / CBRAIN-CAM) widely recognized as an open testbed for offline ML parameterization development and interpretability.
pain_points: Large dimensionality and parameter count in deep neural networks impede physical interpretability and trustworthiness without complex attribution techniques
Lower tropospheric moistening tendencies in the subtropics (descending branch of the Hadley cell) exhibit lower predictive skill due to underrepresentation of convective variability

Standard input-to-output mapping (X -> Y) failed to organize large-scale features cleanly in the latent space; requiring dual reconstruction of X and Y simultaneously to achieve interpretable latent manifolds
Trade-off between compression level (latent space width) and offline predictive accuracy
extraction_notes: The study conducts purely offline training and evaluation using 9 months total (3 months each for space-time shuffled training, unshuffled validation, and unshuffled test data). Online prognostic coupling into SPCAM was not performed in this paper.
